topics.topic: Closed machine-readable refusal reason identifiers, parameters, and mapping from failed checks
questions: What exact machine-readable reason identifiers can accompany `refused`, and how is each failed check mapped to one?
What closed, machine-readable reason identifiers and associated parameters correspond to every operation-specific refusal check?
How are a missing implementation, contract version, source execution, StoredValue or SpooledFile reported by this operation?

judgement.divergence: One implementer returns only the generic `refused` code with free-form bounded text naming a failed check, while another defines stable per-check identifiers and parameters; callers and agents observe different response data and cannot reliably branch on the same failures.
judgement.why: The texts enumerate top-level refusal codes and operation-failure details but never close the identifiers, parameters, or check-to-identifier mapping for operation-specific `refused` reasons.

topics.topic: Input boundary for canonical JSON bytes and duplicate-member detection
questions: What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` so duplicate object members are still observable?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text and parse it so duplicate keys remain detectable, or does surface parse first and reject duplicate keys before passing a value?

judgement.why: This is the same canonical-bytes input and duplicate-member question already judged in P8, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Input representation and duplicate-key detection for canonical_bytes
quotes: canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] Maps a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
precedent.why: State 7 makes canonical_bytes parse raw JSON text, detect duplicate members, and maps its error to invalid_request.

topics.topic: Measurement unit and truncation semantics for masked failure_detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
What unit is the disclosed length: UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, Unicode code points, or another measure?

quotes:
A `failure_detail` of an execution whose class is above `open` is returned to an
   agent only as its length and that class.
judgement.why: The measurement-unit ambiguity is in this unchanged passage, and the reopening change neither touched it nor made the distinction newly consequential.

topics.topic: Representation and persistence of operation-failure codes and response-body diagnostics in NodeExecution
questions: How are the actionable closed code and the optional response-body diagnostic represented in the resulting NodeExecution?
How are both the machine-actionable operation-failure code and a response-body diagnostic represented and persisted, especially for a read answered 3xx?

quotes:
11. **A NodeExecution carries `detail_code`** beside `failure_detail`: the closed
    detail of State 5 is a code, the excerpt is text, and the owner acts on the
    code.

send_under_authority: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The NodeExecutionDraft has status the SendResult outcome name (= models.NodeExecutionStatus), detail_code and failure_detail from the SendResult, executed the ExecutedBinding of the binding, inputs the element's input PortRefs, outputs one StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef per output port in port name order, a SpooledFilesRef with the class the binding declares for that port, and no resources_used.
judgement.why: The later texts give NodeExecution separate `detail_code` and `failure_detail` fields and persist both from the send result.

topics.topic: Allowed service base-URL components and URL joining semantics
questions: Are a base URL's userinfo, query, fragment and path prefix allowed, and is joining literal concatenation or URL-component resolution?

topics.topic: Approval digest and content-length treatment of multipart boundaries
questions: Does a changed multipart boundary invalidate an approval, and how is content-length determined when the boundary that affects the wire body length is excluded from the approved request description?

topics.topic: Cleanup of content-addressed file bytes from changes that never commit
questions: What happens to file bytes copied or published for a change whose record is never committed?

topics.topic: Conclusion and determining records for approval-requested elements without a NodeExecution
questions: When an element has no NodeExecution but has a requested approval, is its conclusion `owner_approval` or `not reached`, and which records determine that distinction?

topics.topic: Durability and later visibility of explicit-try executions
questions: Are explicit try executions durably recorded and visible to later inspection and repair operations, or are they observationally ephemeral?

topics.topic: Eligibility and ordering semantics for the rollback implementation slot
questions: What makes an implementation “earlier”: merely existing and non-current, created before the current implementation, or previously active before the current activation?

topics.topic: Failure-subject locator representation across proof phases
questions: How is the failing subject represented for every proof phase when it is not naturally one node or one existing edge?

topics.topic: Input references recorded for mapped-node aggregate failures
questions: What exact M23 input references does that aggregate NodeExecution contain for the mapped port and the shared ports?

topics.topic: M19 facts included in all run-answer responses
questions: Which M19 facts are returned by `get_run`, `list_records` for runs, and every mutating operation that returns a run answer?

topics.topic: Representation of file input and expected-output bytes in authored trial cases
questions: How does an authored trial case supply the actual bytes of file inputs and expected file outputs?

topics.topic: Representation returned for successful explicit-try value outputs
questions: Does an explicit try return successful non-personal output values, StoredValue references, or only their digests?

topics.topic: Required and permitted trial-case input and expected-output port coverage
questions: Must inputs contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and when expected_outputs is present must it contain exactly every output port, or may expected outputs be partial?

topics.topic: Response processing required for bindings without output ports
questions: For a binding without output ports, must the response body still be read to the ceiling, credential-scanned and classified, with only JSON parsing and output extraction skipped?

topics.topic: Result, cleanup, and accounting when spool-file ceiling-refusal cleanup fails
questions: What happens if removing an earlier file of the same attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal, and what result and spool accounting must the operation expose?

topics.topic: Retry trigger for token-list rereading after an invalid reread
questions: After a failed re-read leaves no valid token list, when is the next re-read attempted, especially if the file is restored to bytes equal to the last successfully loaded file?

topics.topic: Revision-pinned manifest record reads and proof of revision provenance
questions: How is `manifest_revision` applied when reading a record, and what proves that the bytes came from that revision rather than the working tree at `manifest_location`?

topics.topic: Runtime value-output boundary representation and canonicalization ownership
questions: What exact representation crosses from the sandbox and service invoker to the modules that persist value outputs, and which module canonicalizes those values into stored bytes?

topics.topic: Schema and required input facts for constant requests
questions: Does each constant request include its own declared schema, and if so what exact constant input facts are required?

topics.topic: Source of exact input references for refused-by-owner NodeExecutions
questions: Where does decide_effect_approval obtain the exact input references required for the refused_by_owner NodeExecution?

topics.topic: Startup recovery ordering for multiple newly reachable elements in one run
questions: In what order are multiple elements of the same run whose waits ceased to hold reached during startup recovery, before normal advancement begins?

topics.topic: Startup validation and failure-order position for configured service identifiers
questions: Which operation validates service identifiers appearing in `service_instances` and `service_credentials`, and where does that validation fall in the fixed startup failure order?
